thread:
Emma Li: FYI nightly evals for the int4 quantized model are timing out ~30% of runs since last night. Root log shows bind errors when workers start.

Raj Patel: ugh, link to the job?

Emma Li: https://ci.internal/jobs/8245 (job 8245). snippet: 
```
2026-03-19T03:12:11.234Z worker-manager INFO starting worker pid=1284
2026-03-19T03:12:11.241Z worker ERROR failed to bind control socket: [Errno 98] Address already in use
2026-03-19T03:12:16.678Z harness WARN worker startup timed out, killing pid=1284
```

Santiago Ruiz: Address already in use during bind on ephemeral port? Are we specifying a fixed port or letting OS pick one?

Emma Li: harness uses `bind(('', 0))` and then reads `getsockname()` to learn the port, then writes port to a tmpfile for the parent. Seems like the bind itself is failing with EADDRINUSE.

Maya Chen: that usually means either another process is bound to the same port, or there's a reuse race with TIME_WAIT on the socket. But when binding to 0 OS should choose a free port. Do we fork before binding?

Raj Patel: I ran a repro locally with 20 parallel workers. Reproduced ~10% of the time: two processes get the same port number returned due to a race in the tmpfile write operation — parent reads stale tmpfile before child actually binds.

Emma Li: here's the sequence I suspect: parent launches child -> child picks port N but crashes before bind -> parent sees tmpfile with port N (or reads a value from a previous run) and then another child tries to bind and gets EADDRINUSE. Logs show a 1-2s window where multiple workers think port N is reserved.

Santiago Ruiz: can you paste the harness snippet that writes the tmpfile?

Emma Li: sure:
```
# child
s.bind((host, 0))
port = s.getsockname()[1]
open(tmpfile, 'w').write(str(port))
# parent
port = int(open(tmpfile).read())
connect(host, port)
```

Maya Chen: That write/read without any atomic handshake is brittle under parallel CI job reuse and flaky cleanup. If the child crashes after writing but before binding, we get a stale port. Also race if tmpfile path reused across parallel test shards.

Raj Patel: We also saw recently that CI concurrency bumped from 10->30 on eng-ml runners last week. That probably increased collisions.

infra-bot: runner-update: eng-ml concurrency = 30 (changed 2026-03-18 22:05 UTC)

Santiago Ruiz: short-term mitigation: make tmpfile unique per worker (use pid or uuid), and add a handshake where parent polls the child's pid and waits until a short 'ready' ack is present. Also set socket option `SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE` or use unix domain sockets.

Emma Li: quick patch posted: https://phab/internal/D12345 includes unique tmpfile and explicit `s.listen(1)` before writing the port. Testing now on a small matrix.

Raj Patel: alternative longer-term fix: switch harness IPC to unix domain sockets under /tmp/harness-sockets/<job-id>/, avoids ephemeral port pool entirely. Any infra reasons not to?

Maya Chen: cross-host tests won't work with unix sockets, but these are single-host workers. For cross-host we should use an allocator service that reserves ports centrally. That feels heavier. I like unix sockets for most harness flows.

Emma Li: running a 200-run stress with the quick patch applied — 0/200 failures so far (was ~30/100 before). Will leave stress running overnight.

Santiago Ruiz: thanks. Can you also add a CI job that runs the stress after any harness changes? Add a flake-alert to page eng-ml if failure rate > 1% for 1h.

Emma Li: added a canary: ci-bot will trigger nightly-stress after deploy.

ci-bot: scheduled nightly-stress for branch D12345, will report failures in #eng-ml-canary

Raj Patel: follow-up: if this is the root cause we should also audit other places using tmpfiles for port exchange (model-onboarding scripts, local dev harnesses). I can grep.

Maya Chen: I'll lower concurrency on the runners to 20 as a precaution and open a ticket to expand the ephemeral port range on the infra side if needed.

Emma Li: thanks everyone — keeping thread updated. If the overnight stress stays green I'll merge the quick patch tomorrow and schedule the unix-socket refactor for next sprint. :thumbsup:
